metadata.title: Dividend Aristocrats: revenue and earnings growth
methodology: Universe: the 69 S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats reflected in dated September 29, 2026 ProShares NOBL holdings, excluding the three REITs ESS, FRT and O. The holdings are cross-checked against S&P index information; fund cash is excluded.

Annual GAAP revenue and diluted EPS from continuing operations. FY2025 is the common fiscal-year endpoint, compared with FY2020 and FY2005. Fiscal calendars differ; exact period-end dates are retained.

All 66 FY2025 annual reports are available as of the research date. Some issuers already have FY2026 annual results, which are noted; the common FY2025 endpoint avoids mixing fiscal-year labels. No FY2025 filing is flagged as outstanding.

A pass requires BOTH ending revenue and ending diluted continuing-operations EPS to exceed their starting values. This is cumulative endpoint growth, not annual growth every year or positive profit in every intervening year.

Growth percentages use end/base - 1 only when the starting value is positive. Zero and negative starting EPS retain dollar-per-share endpoints and are evaluated as improvement or decline; no conventional percentage or CAGR is invented.

Latest available annual-filing comparative figures as of September 30, 2026 are used for recent endpoints. Historical manual entries identify their filing and reporting scope. Revenue taxonomy selection favors total GAAP revenue, with issuer-specific concepts documented.

Where only total diluted EPS is tagged, continuing-operations equivalence is verified against the same filing using an explicit zero discontinued-operations amount, income-statement review, or a retained pretax/tax/net-income reconciliation within reported rounding.

EPS is placed on a consistent share basis. True share splits and reverse splits are distinguished from market-data price adjustments for spin-offs. Underlying historical figures, factors, corporate-action sources and raw evidence are retained.

Spin-offs, mergers, acquisitions, disposals, accounting changes and currency effects can alter reporting scope. These are as-reported GAAP comparisons, not organic growth or a constant-business reconstruction.

Short histories are shown separately using the earliest supportable audited company or carve-out values. They never count as full five- or twenty-year passes. Missing evidence remains incomplete; no estimates are substituted.
This is a dated financial screen, not a stock-price return backtest or a recommendation. Current-constituent selection means it does not describe the experience of buying the index twenty years ago.

Reporting-basis sensitivity: ExxonMobil and Chevron's twenty-year revenue results change direction if specifically disclosed historical excise taxes and gross buy/sell transactions are removed. Main classifications follow reported GAAP sales, with illustrative alternatives separately labeled. Brown-Forman also changed excise-tax presentation. These comparisons are not uniformly like-for-like.
